items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: And then when Red came along I listened to Red.

ctx.x: By ear? When you started doing the vibes —

Well yeah. Nobody could teach me. So what I did, I was taking piano lessons, I adopted the right hand of the piano, all the exercises and what-have-you, and basically taught myself by listening to Hampton really. And then when Red came along I listened to Red. And then there was one guy that played, Art Van Damme. He was a good player. I started to get a few of his records, and I think there was a group called the Merry Mac Singers, they had a vibraphone player. It wasn’t very popular. It wasn’t heard that much.…
Were records back then a precious commodity? I mean were they precious?
